options.text: Admonish [character] for his behavior.
I have enjoyed the sultry display.
Demand an apology from [character].
Show no reaction whatsoever.

events.text: During a goodwill banquet with courtiers from [rival], your husband appears to be flirting quite openly with [character]. When confronted, he dismisses your concerns. The dalliance continues for the rest of the evening, causing much heated gossip between the two courts.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: A Friend In Need

options.text: Yes, but [rival] will owe us a favor.
Your ships must find their own way home.

events.text: Reports of lost [rival] ships arrive from the coast, following by a desperate messenger. "Our navigators have grossly overestimated their abilities, and our shipments are scattered across the seas. Please, can you help us?" Should we share our expertise with [rival]?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Generous Donation

options.text: We will gladly take any assistance you can offer.
That deal is not acceptable.

events.text: A message arrives from [character]. He has not forgotten your kind gestures toward him and wishes to return the favor. [rival] agents have reported our recent struggles with the wood supply. He is willing to offer a generous donation of wood, but he does not want to offend us with charity. [rival] will accept a gift of our current scientific research in exchange.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Gift of Labor

options.text: We need farms to grow food.
We need mines to gather ore.
We need quarries to harvest stone.
Please keep your gifts.

events.text: Visitors to the court notice a caravan of strange wagons filling the streets outside. It comes to our attention that this group of travelers is a contingent of [rival] sent as a gesture of thanks from [character]. He wishes to express his appreciation to us for aiding [rival] in its time of greatest need. The caravan includes laborers instructed to build whatever we require, as repayment of our favor.

events.text: An envoy from [rival] has come to tell you that [character] is very upset with your ongoing cordial relations with [rival]. “Your continued tolerance for those fools in [rival] presents us with many difficulties,” he says, “but a gift would make this easier to accept.”

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: A Jealous Suitor

options.text: Then I take the hand of [rival].
[rival] shall be my choice.
The more dancers the merrier the dance!

events.text: An ambassador has arrived from [rival] to say that our continued friendship with [rival] jeopardizes our relationship with them. “You cannot dance with two partners,” he says, “you must choose one. And [rival] is a fine dancer!”

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Personal Letter

options.text: Host our nobles in the capital for a feast.
Share some of your latest discoveries with us.
Agree to a trade deal with our merchants.
You need only ask.

events.text: In an effusive and intimate letter, [character] longs for a time when he could call you friend. "How might I mend this rift?" he wonders. "I would do nearly anything to feel close to you again." The court has some ideas...

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: A Plea for Knowledge

options.text: We are happy to share with our neighbors.
Agree to their request... for a price.
Refuse to entertain such an idea.

events.text: Gasps of shock and surprise spread around the court as the [rival] diplomat prostrates himself on the ground in supplication. "Our nation has much to learn. We humbly ask that you share your knowledge with us, so that we may move forwards as friends." Will you give [rival] a gift of technology?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: A Spiritual Connection

options.text: A nation must unite under one spiritual truth.
We welcome [religion], but it does not rule us.
We do not want foreign faiths spreading in our cities.

events.text: A message arrives from [character]. Stories of the savage [rival] nation have reached him in the court of [rival]. "One cannot lead if one cannot see the light of faith," he advises. [character] urges you to accept [religion] as a State Religion, as he has done.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: A Time to Kill

options.text: The sooner he’s dead the better!
Let us try to remain undetected.
I spoke in haste, say no more about this.

events.text: During a discussion about how to deal with [nation] you make it clear that you wish someone would rid you of this turbulent [character]. Unexpectedly, everyone is in agreement and soon practical matters are being hammered out. The only question which remains is should we focus on stealth or speed?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: A Tiny Favor

options.text: [rival] can be trusted with our secrets.
Some knowledge is best kept to ourselves.

events.text: Several officers of the [rival] military appear before the court with a message. "Our mighty ruler, [character], suggests that you share with us your most effective metalworking secrets. Sharing this knowledge will show your willingness to cooperate with us." What is our response?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Aligned Interests

options.text: Whatever the reasons, better [character] deal than scrapping negotiations.
I am not sure who this arrangement benefits, but it's not [rival].

events.text: [rival] funds for [rival] crops. [character] has been pushing this deal, hard. You ponder such single-minded determination on the issue. Some entanglement with [rival] politics? Related business interests? Pure stubbornness?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Allied Intelligence

options.text: Smuggle them in with trade shipments.
Ask the [tribe] to provide safe passage.
Send an official [rival] escort across the border.
It's best not to risk anything.

events.text: Our supporter [character] has come to us with valuable information. His agents in [rival] have discovered a cache of unfinished maps that show the farthest reaches of the nation's borders. [character] will have the maps brought to the court, but getting the spies out of [rival] will not be easy.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: An Admirer

options.text: This is the perfect opportunity to connect our nations.
If [rival] hosts, [rival] will send representatives.
We cannot afford such silly frivolities.

events.text: You receive an eloquent personal letter from [character], ruler of [rival]. He confesses to having read your various writings on government, philosophy, and art, and he is understandably impressed. [character] wishes to establish a joint cultural program with scholars of [rival], a venture that would enrich both nations. It would mean much to [character] personally.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: An Upgrade

options.text: We will trade knowledge for fresh conscripts.
No. A roof over their heads is enough.

events.text: Several landowners from the nation of [rival] seek an audience. They complain about the shabbiness and instability of their cottages, and desire to learn our methods of crafting larger, sturdier manor homes. Shall we share this knowledge?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: An Urgent Matter!

options.text: Good riddance, infected Wood!
This seems suspicious, fetch the royal Entomologist! Recall that Wood!
Pretend to have fallen for this Scheme, but have the Wood sabotaged before it reaches [rival].

events.text: An agent of [character] has arrived in the dead of night with a dire warning! She reveals that [rival] spies uncovered a nefarious plot directed against us. It seems that our enemies have sabotaged our latest wood shipment with some kind of voracious wood-eating beetle in a ploy to infect and ruin our entire wood stockpile. These beetles are also highly vicious and venomous, so the agent doesn’t recommend any of our men get too close to the shipment. The beetles are extremely rapid reproducers who will spread throughout our lands if the wood were simply dumped, and also produce a noxious smoke if burned. The agent has only one solution: She has redirected the Wood shipment to [rival] where they have a special acid which can dissolve the wood and beetles harmlessly. [character], in his benevolence, asks for nothing in return. Indeed he is grateful for the opportunity to destroy such a scourge.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Ancestral Claim

options.text: Raise a militia in the city to scare off the diplomats.
I will show them how to take a city.
Refuse to risk raising tensions.
Maybe he should have [city].

events.text: The 'diplomats' of [character] have arrived in [city], greatly disturbing the [family]. They worry that the foreign ruler is attempting to lay claim to the city, fabricating an ancestral connection to the land it is built on. [character] comes before you, begging that you take action to prevent the city from being taken.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Antichrist

options.text: They speak the truth. Beware [character], beware the false prophet!
[family] theology should not get into the way of diplomacy with [rival].

events.text: Word has reached you that [family] priests are starting their daily prayers by denouncing [character] of [rival] as the Antichrist. They claim he is the prophesied man of sin whose lawlessness and duplicity shall soon be revealed. It will not take long for this to become known in [rival] unless the [family] prayers change.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Appealing Argument

options.text: They make a compelling point.
Any argument can be refuted!

events.text: Recently preachers of [religion] have turned up in [city]. Rather than trying to use fear or offers of unconditional love, they are employing an incredibly reasonable argument which is convincing many citizens to convert.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Appealing Argument

options.text: They make a compelling point.
Any argument can be refuted!

events.text: Recently preachers of [religion] have turned up in [city]. Rather than trying to use fear or offers of unconditional love, they are employing an incredibly reasonable argument which is convincing many citizens to convert.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Arming Your Brothers

options.text: Give them what they want.
Placate them with a gift of iron instead.
No, we cannot let [rival] become too powerful.

events.text: The news of [rival] military advancements have traveled across the world, whispered about on the road and discussed by foreign generals. Impressed by the tales of such technological achievements, the friendly nation of [rival] has sent a delegation of officials to ask if we would be willing to share our knowledge with them. Shall we help to arm our friends, or is the risk of these weapons turning against us too great?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: At Death's Door

options.text: Do not fear, I will send my royal healer.
Our doctors will send their best treatments.
You have my prayers and... condolences.
I will arrange a visit and see to him myself.

events.text: Ambassadors from [rival] seek a private audience. Behind closed doors, they deliver somber news from [character]. His son has taken ill on a trip to [city] and is dying. "We have had our differences," he explains in the letter, "but I request your aid in this difficult time." How will you reply?

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Avoiding Tensions

options.text: "Now is the time to write a Peace treaty to ensure our future co-operation."
"If we share some of our knowledge with you, will that erase these complaints?"
"I am too busy planning the design of my next Library building to bother with you at the moment."

events.text: An emissary from [rival], with whom we have good relations, has brought a list of grievances against our nation. While they downplay the current impact of these grievances, the suggestion is clear that if not addressed satisfactorily, these types of issues could lead to tensions in the future.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Awaiting Execution

options.text: Engage in diplomatic negotiations with [rival].
This is not a priority for the court.
Send spies to arrange for the prisoner's escape.

events.text: Local [religion] priests have received dire messages from their counterparts in [rival]. The [rival] [title], [character], has imprisoned a [religion] missionary team and is making plans for their execution. Apparently, these devout followers failed to win [character]'s favor. The priests urge us to take action.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Bad Blood

options.text: Warn [rival] to deal with the court... not with individuals.
Invite [character] to a private dinner of political allies.
Order spies to monitor him.

events.text: [character] has been witnessed meeting privately with agents of [rival], but we do not know the subject of these discussions. It may be wise to bring him back under our influence. If not, we should assign agents to track his movements. What do you command?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Battle Plans

options.text: We must use everything we can against our rivals.
Such treachery sets a dangerous precedent.

events.text: In an intelligence triumph, our spies have discovered the battle plans for the [rival] military. This new information could severely hinder their ambitions... if used to our advantage. Of course, the court is divided over whether to use this knowledge. [character] insists that [rival] will wage war on us eventually, and that it is wise to be prepared. Others, however, view using the intelligence as unethical, even villainous.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Between Us

options.text: Make this happen for [character].
Sharing goes both ways.
Share, but give him faulty information.
Our science is a national secret.

events.text: During a recent visit, [character] speaks of nothing else but the impressive horse armor flaunted by our highest generals. He sends a messenger to speak with you in private, inquiring about securing armor of his own. We would need to share our discovery of Barding. Do we want to set a precedent of sharing national secrets for personal favor?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Blame Game

options.text: Agree with [character]. Weakness breeds defeat.
Agree with [character]. Conflict is not the solution.
Say nothing, and suggest a short break in negotiations.

events.text: A mission from [rival] arrives in court eager to discuss recent tensions. Both [character] and his heir, [character], are in attendance. During the debates, [character] turns on [character] and blames his younger generation for "lashing the dogs of war." In response, the heir accuses the [title] of weakness in the face of his rivals. The pair turns to you, each expecting validation.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Boastful Heir

options.text: [character]'s youth reveals his great ignorance.
Without a doubt, [character] is a laughingstock.
You rule well, and so will [character] one day.

events.text: The royal family of [rival] visits the court. During a feast, [character] makes a shocking boast about how much better a ruler he will be one day. [character] chides him for his brashness and turns to us for support. What do we say?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Bonded by Faith

options.text: Join in an alliance with [rival].
Reject the alliance. You will meet [rival] on your own terms.
This is a perfect opportunity to weaken [rival]. Attack!

events.text: You have been asked by [character] to meet at a remote temple on the border of your lands. Arriving with your retinue, you are surprised to find that he is with [character]. [character] explains to you both that he is hoping that your two nations will agree to be bonded in an alliance before. You look over at [character]. He looks surprised, but seems open to the idea. How will you respond?

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Bound by Blood

options.text: Commission an epic retelling of your royal lines.
Accept the gift and promise friendship.
Refuse to acknowledge any ties between your lines.

events.text: The diplomats from [rival] present a gift of a sword, lavishly inlaid with jewels and an inscription in some long-forgotten form of. They explain that [character] scholars now believe that your lines are connected by a shared ancestor,.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Bow Before Us

options.text: No one chooses our faith for us.
Honor the visitors with a celebration.
Establish [religion] as our state religion.
[rival] should try [religion].

events.text: A retinue of ambassadors, priests, and officers have arrived from [rival] with a message of hope. The great [title], [character], has issued a call for all nations to establish [religion] as their State Religion, spreading the teachings of the prophets across the world. Our visitors require an answer.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Campaign Planning

options.text: Focus on training drills and exercises.
Send the word out, the next campaign will be against [rival].

requirements.label: Charming character / Prosperous
tip: The leader must have one of: Charming character (a character trait); Prosperous

options.text: Send the generals to defend the roads and trade routes.

events.text: It is a time of peace, but without anything to do the generals start to become restless. [character] is concerned that the peace could be mistaken for weakness, and suggests giving a clear direction for the generals to work towards. What instructions will you give?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Cancel Trade

options.text: We will stop trading with [rival].
[rival] will not be told what to do.

events.text: A messenger arrives with a stern warning from [character]. [rival] is displeased with our ongoing trade with [rival], their hated enemy. They demand that we cease all transfer of goods and services immediately. What is our reply?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Capsized Spies

options.text: Publicly accuse the [family] of treason.
Ignore the involvement and blame [rival].
Keep the affair quiet, and make [character] a double-agent.

events.text: The morning after a terrible storm, guards discover a capsized sailboat swept up on the coast near a [family] estate. After several hours of intense interrogation, the survivors admit to spying for the leadership of [rival]. They claim that [character] is working in concert with the [rival] to bring about the court's demise. What shall we do about this?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Citizenship

options.text: Gold is a fair price to pay for citizenship.
We do not wish to meddle in [rival]'s affairs.

events.text: Vagabonds in several [rival] cities are requesting to be officially recognized by the state. Are we willing to share the concept of citizenship with [rival]? This act may generate goodwill among people of both our nations. What shall we do?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Condolences

options.text: Please send [character] my eternal gratitude.
You cannot buy my goodwill with gifts.

events.text: News of your recent loss reaches beyond our borders. As a result, an emissary arrives from [rival] with a gift from [character]. He describes it as "a simple gesture, to show our condolences." But is anything in this world a simple gesture? Your Ambassador, [character], suspects that this goodwill is a ruse to earn your gratitude, easing tensions.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Converting the Heir

options.text: Gift him with a lavish scroll of teachings.
Encourage the inquisitive heir to go to [character] with any more questions.

events.text: On a diplomatic visit to your court, the royal family of [rival] sit beside you as honored guests for the evening feast. The heir, [character], is intrigued by your jewelry with [religion] imagery. As the meal concludes, he asks for a text to learn more about the religion. A staunch [religion], [character] is unlikely to take kindly to you influencing [character]. What reply will you give?

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Convincing Case

options.text: We cannot argue with that.
Reject their illogical ramblings!

events.text: [rival] proselytizers have appeared in [city] bearing the writ of [character]. Cunning legal arguments direct the citizens of [city] to convert to [religion] immediately on pain of censure.

events.author: David Ballantyne
events.name: Convincing Case

options.text: We cannot argue with that.
Reject their illogical ramblings!

events.text: [rival] proselytizers have appeared in [city] bearing the writ of [character]. Well researched arguments direct the citizens of [city] to convert to [religion] immediately on pain of censure.

events.author: Solver
events.name: Culinary Diplomacy

options.text: The proposal is as generous as it is useful.
[character] humbles me and has my gratitude, but we shall pay from the treasury.
Send the goods, and add this fruit that few in [rival] or [rival] know.

events.text: Ambassador [character] has been doing some research on the personal habits of [character]. As luck would have it, [character] is quite partial to certain delicacies we have in abundance here in [rival]. [character] sees this is a good opportunity to improve relations with [rival]. Moreover, as a sign of his personal gratitude to you, [character] offers to pay for the delicacy shipment himself.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Deadly Inheritance

options.text: Reveal the conspiracy to [character].
Let events play out as they must.

leadsTo.name: I Love It When A Plan Comes Together!

options.text: Approach [character] about joining the plot.

events.text: [character] and his heir, [character], descend on our capital for a surprise visit. Celebrations are held, and the visitors enjoy a restful evening among the elite. However, our agents have uncovered disturbing rumors of a plot against [character]'s life. The conspirators are followers of the heir, [character], and they plan to kill the [title] during the visit, to cloak their identities and sow confusion.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Denouncement

options.text: The court will denounce [rival].
No, we must choose our battles.
I will remind them of [rival]'s sovereign rights.

events.text: Members of the [family] family vehemently oppose [rival]'s decision to adopt [law], and they request that we make a formal denouncement. Not everyone in the court agrees with the [family] so we should consider our next move carefully.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Dinner with Rivals

options.text: I agree. [character] is the superior general.
Let us be realistic. Everyone knows [character] is unbeatable.
Surely, it is foolish to compare mortals and immortals!

events.text: A delegation from [rival] is sent to help settle a minor dispute that is brewing between your two nations. At dinner, one of their party speculates on who could beat the gods of war, leading to a spirited debate. They put forward [character] as the best candidate. Some other visiting dignitaries from [rival] suggest [character]. Whom do you choose?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Dinner with a Rival

options.text: I agree. [character] is the most superior general.
Let's be realistic. Everyone knows our own [character] is unbeatable.
Surely, it is foolish to compare mortals and immortals!

events.text: A delegation from [rival] is sent to help settle a minor dispute that is brewing between your two nations. At dinner, one of their party speculates on who could beat the gods of war, leading to a spirited debate. They put forward [character] as the best candidate. Who do you choose?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Diplomatic Discussions

options.text: Our humility endears us to both.
Not right now.

events.text: Court diplomats have been hard at work on discussions with representatives from both [rival] and [rival], but they wish to focus their efforts. Which nation should they seek to influence, [rival] or [rival]?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Diplomatic Match

options.text: [character] will make a fine husband.
[character] will make a fine husband.
I will not choose right now.

events.text: [rival] matchmakers have arrived, hoping to arrange a royal marriage for [character]. Who shall wed [character]?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Diplomatic Mission

options.text: Have them come for an audience with the court.
Never, we will not play host to our enemies!
There is much to discuss with the [rival].

events.text: Dignitaries from [rival] are passing through the region on a diplomatic mission. [character] wishes to host them at the palace. It is no secret that tensions are high with the [rival], but perhaps a royal visit will help cooler heads prevail.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Disrespect

options.text: Stains are easier to remove than invading armies.
Would you care to draft the court's response then, [character]?

events.text: From the look on [character] face, you would think the [rival] were demanding firstborn children, rather than iron shipments. "Does [character] really think [rival] is so weak as to grovel at his passing whim? Any response but to spit in his face would be too kind and a stain on [rival] honor."

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Disturbing the Peace

outcomes.label: Trait Disturbing The Peace Option 0 Ruthless
Trait Disturbing The Peace Option 0 Cruel
Trait Disturbing The Peace Option 0 Intolerant

options.text: A little torture never hurt anyone.
Demand a ransom from [character].
I will win the heir's affections.

events.text: By chance, the heir of your rival, [character] of [rival], has been caught disturbing the peace in the outskirts of [city]. He is notorious for his foreign holidays and drunken exploits. What shall we do with [character]? He is quickly aggravating every other prisoner in the city jail.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Divine Mission

options.text: Fund a grand mission with gifts of food, incense, and religious texts for them to read.
Send a more modest mission, aiming to delay any thought of hostilities.

events.text: The [rival], with whom we have no serious conflict, appear to be growing restless. Some say their view of us is on the decline. Perhaps it is time to send a mission to their lands and to spread our spiritual beliefs.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Division in the Faith

options.text: Very well.
No, they have every right to their beliefs.

events.text: The [rival] ambassador approaches with all due reverence, appearing before you with little ceremony. He delivers the message from [character], who claims that the people of [rival] have taken to perverting [religion] beliefs with their own forms of magic and superstition. [character] makes an offer for your two nations to enter into a formal Peace, if you declare war on [rival].

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Era of Peace

options.text: Establish trade routes with [rival] to further secure the peace.
Strengthen ties with [rival] by inviting one of their nobles to our court.
Take advantage of our neighbors’ naivety by stealing their secrets.

events.text: In recent seasons, a sense of calm has settled over the land. Free from the devastation of war, we share with our neighbors a sentiment of hope. How will you lead [rival] forward during these times of peace?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Exchange of Ideas

options.text: Yes, if they can spare a philosopher.
Science is meant to be shared.
Some secrets will shall keep to ourselves.

events.text: Great scientist [character] has been exchanging messages with his counterpart on the [rival] court, and he believes we have much to gain from sharing our Scholarship with them. Is the exchange of ideas worth the risk to national security?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Face in Gold

options.text: This privilege is reserved for the true [title] - me.
It is only right that they pay for their coinage.
The [rival] must be willing to trade.

tip: As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Siege
As leader: +10% Unit Trait Modifier / Ship

options.text: I have always held your cities in high esteem.

events.text: Not long after the first coins with your kingly visage appear in the streets of [city], emissaries from [rival] request a meeting. It seems their ruler, [character], wishes to see his own face staring back at him in gold. We will organize a meeting to discuss Coinage with the [rival], but they must be willing to negotiate.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Faith Without Borders

options.text: Accept the teachings in the scrolls.
Make a show of burning the scrolls.
Explain that you are bound by duty to your state religion.

events.text: A man of faith, [character] is known to be a staunch follower of [religion]. For weeks now, the uncompromising ruler has been sending messengers with gifts of expensively bound and illustrated [religion] texts. The noble families are worried about this foreign influence, begging for the scrolls to be destroyed. Although it would anger your state religion of [religion], a show of following [character] religion could be a fast way to make friends.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Faith and Unity

options.text: Very well. For the time being, we shall set aside our differences and call an end to the fighting.
We will end hostilities when I decide, and not a moment sooner. I will bow to pressure from no one.

events.text: You have had devastating success in the field in your war against [rival]. Unfortunately, your armies have been so efficient and effective that it is raising some alarms. Recently, [character] the head of your [religion] faith has been making impassioned pleas that the hostilities against your brothers and sisters of [rival] and questions have begun circulating as to why you are not focusing the attention of your armies against the heathens. Victory is close, but pressing your advantage will mean alienating [character]. How do you wish to proceed?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Favor for a Favor

options.text: We could always use another talented merchant in our inner circle.
We'll call our favor repaid in exchange for the services of a skilled General.
No. For the moment, at least, we'll hold onto that favor.

events.text: [character] contacts you somewhat unexpectedly. "I am in your debt, and would like to repay your previous kindness to me and mine. Would you consider accepting one of my talented Courtiers into your own ranks as payment in full? Your choice, naturally." It is an intriguing idea...

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Feast or Famine

options.text: [rival] can spare nothing, lest we suffer the same fate.
Offer a gift of Food to the struggling [rival].
We will trade with [rival].
Let’s trade, yes, and we will dictate the terms.

events.text: Though Food supplies in [rival] remain plentiful in spite of the [event], not all nations are faring so well. An envoy arrives from [rival], and you quickly learn of their plight. [character] is humbly asking for assistance. Perhaps there is something to be gained from the situation.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Fighting for [rival]

options.text: Disparage [character] for recruiting your best people.
Celebrate the departure of such a weak, cowardly fool.
Employ your military connections to find and target [character].

events.text: Suffering from one too many disappointments, [character] has chosen to take his grievances abroad. In the dead of night, he and his family slip across the border with possessions in tow, assisted by servants of several powerful [rival] families. [character] receives an appointment in the [rival] military almost immediately after arriving. His expertise will serve [rival] well.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Foiled Assassin

options.text: [character] wants blood? We will give him blood.
Double the guard for [character], but take no rash action for now.
Send assassins to plague [character]'s family.

events.text: Palace guards apprehend an intruder just outside your husband's chambers. The woman carries a dagger, and wears clothing meant to conceal her in the shadows. She will not answer our questions, but appears to be [rival]. The only plausible explanation is that we've just foiled an assassin sent by [character]!

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Food for Peace

options.text: Send a shipment of Food, to provide immediate relief.

requirements.label: Builder / Engineer / Carpenter
tip: The leader must have one of: Builder; Engineer; Carpenter

options.text: Send a team of builders to construct a Granary at a location of their choice.

requirements.label: Inquisitive
tip: The leader must have Inquisitive (a character trait)

options.text: Offer them insights into how our Farms and Pastures are constructed and organized.
Refuse.

events.text: Emissaries arrive from [rival], with whom we have good relations. "Our people struggle to feed ourselves, while yours seem to have plenty. This is creating a growing sense of tension on our side. Perhaps you should send us shipments of food in tribute."

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Food for Thought

options.text: We will send them a gift of food.
Encourage our farmers to share our techniques to save the animals they have.
This is not our problem.

events.text: Some progress comes from great minds exploring their theoretical worlds, some comes from honest people doing their best to get by. The farmers of [rival] are proud of our nation's skills at Husbandry and fine pastures. The advancements in agriculture have naturally started to spread, with [rival] coming close to our skills at raising animals. However, word comes that they have been hit by a plague that has wiped out much of their livestock and ask that you send aid.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Foreign Bribes

options.text: Send [character] into distant exile.
Accuse [rival] of influencing the court.
Pay off [character]'s debts to earn his favor.

events.text: Court spies witness the great minister [character] accepting bribes from agents of [rival]. It seems that he owes money to individuals across the capital. [rival] has been paying him to champion policy favorable to its people in court. What shall be done?

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Funds for the Faith

options.text: We will fund their efforts.
We have no spare funds for [religion].

events.text: Missionaries from [rival] have arrived in the capital to raise funds for the ongoing spread of [religion] in [city]. Many in our nation share these beliefs, and it would be wise to pledge more support. What shall we tell them?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Give an inch

options.text: We will never bow to foreign pressure.
[character] is right, and we must restrict freedoms.
I was pressured into these policies by the [family].

events.text: An envoy enters the capital, bearing a message from [character]. The [title] expresses his frustration with our recent laws. "Freedom will prove problematic. Give your subjects any liberties and they will only hunger for more." [character] urges you to reconsider your policies.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Godless

options.text: We are godless and have lost our way.
Our way of life will not be questioned.
Throw feasts in his honor, and he will change his mind.

events.text: [character] visits [rival] and eagerly enjoys a tour of the capital, but he grows silent at the sight of our empty shrines and temples. Back at court, he express a sadness at our secular ways. "It pains me greatly to see [rival] turn away from the sacred." [character]'s comments inspire reflection. [rival] governs with strict Divine Rule, but there is no arguing with the results.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Going for the Head

options.text: Let [rival] know they have your support.
Let [rival] know of the impending danger.

events.text: Your agents have met with the [rival] spymaster, who is making a move to gain power in [religion] by assassinating the [rival] head of the religion, [character], and replacing him with their own candidate, [character]. [rival] trusts that you will support them as they need your agents to secure the religious coup. There is little time to act. Warning [rival] will likely see [rival]’s candidate killed and they would know that you thwarted them. But letting your agents take part in the coup would raise suspicion that you were involved.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Gratitude

options.text: As a tutor for your children and heirs.
As military counsel for our generals and officers.
As a money counter and treasurer.
As a deft mind for science and philosophy.

options.text: Pay the fine, but issue a warning to the [family].

Remind [rival] of the favor they owe us.
Demand the release of our citizens!

events.text: A [family] family hunting party has been arrested for trespassing on land belonging to the [rival], with whom we are at peace. [rival] holds the trespassers in custody and demands a fine for their release. How shall we respond?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: In the Blood

options.text: Share some of our knowledge with [rival].
Let us begin with a military alliance.
A friendship is not in our nation's best interest.

events.text: Generals of the powerful [rival] military parade through our capital, led by the [title] himself, [character]. He has come to treat with you personally. The surprise visit stems from [character]'s desire to improve relations, especially since you are both renowned commanders. Warfare is in your blood.

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Inner Circle

options.text: I welcome [rival] at the court.
No, we must not create conflicts of interest.

events.text: A message arrives from [character]. Having heard rumors of our "small, ineffectual court," he offers to send an advisor to join your inner circle. Obviously, our government is scandalized by such an offer. [rival]? At court?

[character] is unable to fully fund the construction himself and so is selling partial ownership to trusted investors. While initially the only return will be the goodwill of [character], once the bridge is fully funded and allowing for construction costs and a reasonable profit margin for [character], we will be entitled to a share of the crossing tolls proportional to our investment. We’re practically guaranteed to make a huge profit if we can spare a few resources!

events.author: Solver
events.name: Judicial Overreach

options.text: Generous compensation to [rival] should settle the issue.
Apologize and offer our assurances that [character] will be publicly reprimanded.
The [rival] broke the law in [city], where [character]'s authority is unquestionable.

events.text: A trader from [rival] was caught stealing from a local market in [city]. He only stole one fruit, but [character] ordered the man to be immediately put to death. [character] is dismayed at the swift execution, claiming the punishment did not fit the crime. Given our close relations, [rival] would nonetheless be willing to overlook [character]'s idea of justice.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Knowledge of Power

options.text: Send him to learn what he can.
[character] time is better spent training our troops.

events.text: [character] approaches, brow furrowed in thought. He gruffly shares that he has been approached by the [rival] military, who have asked [character] to visit and to help with training a new army. Although not initially tempted, [character] wonders if it could be a chance to learn more of their technologies and training techniques.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Leveraging Luxuries

options.text: We could certainly see our way clear to do that if it means adding a new merchant to the Court.
We would happily make that trade for the opportunity to add a new minister to the Court.
No. We'll keep our luxuries for the time being.

events.text: [rival] contacts you with an intriguing proposal. If you'd be willing to part with some of your luxuries, they'll happily round out your Court with either a talented trader or minister. What say you?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Lost in Translation

options.text: It's clear a landowner needs both male and female cattle. The [rival] is right.
The [rival] is the seller and knows better what he sold.
We can exchange some of our own cattle with the [rival].
We have great independent judges who can find a fair solution.

events.text: [rival] and [rival] have asked us to mediate a contract dispute. A wealthy [rival] bought land and cattle in [rival], with the contract written and sealed by both parties. The buyer only got male cattle, though his contract says in some should be male and some female. The [rival] seller says his copy of the contract clearly states male cattle only. It seems there was a translation issue, and the contract says different things in different languages!

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Map Dispute

options.text: Make a generous contribution to [rival]'s stockpile.
Cancel all friendly ties with the [tribe].
Offer to train his heir in our court.
Refuse to act and have our borders revealed.

events.text: We have received troubling news from [rival]. Soldiers along their border have captured a pair of [tribe] spies carrying detailed maps of [rival]. This information could prove disastrous to our national security. [character] knows he has us in a compromising position and offers several options.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Martial Code

options.text: Yes, share our knowledge of Martial Code.
No, our secrets must be protected.

events.text: A great scientist from the [rival] court of [character] has come to us, seeking assistance with a project. She would like to construct high, protective Towers, like ours, but she lacks some of the fundamental knowledge. Shall we share these discoveries with [rival]?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Martial Trade

options.text: We ask that one of you joins our court.
Our archers could use improved arrows.
This is not a time for trade.

events.text: A mission of [rival] diplomats arrives with [character]'s blessing. They seek advice on how to unite disparate clans under a unifying system. They have heard stories of our Martial Code, and they are open to trading valuable items to understand this way of life. What shall we tell them?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Mechanical Wonders

options.text: Remember this favor when you become king.
This technology is much too valuable to share.
What will they offer [rival] in return?
I am always interested in the finer things.

events.text: [character], the heir to the [rival] throne, makes a surprise visit to the capital. He spends much of his time in the workshop of the great thinker [character], studying the marvelous contraptions devised by our scientists. [character] is very interested in learning more about the wonders of Machinery, and he is willing to pay for it.

events.author: Bob Thomas
events.name: Misdirection

options.text: Spare no expense.
It is best not to risk a scheme that might backfire on us.

events.text: Although the [rival] have a strong positive opinion of us, your agents report that there may be a plot at work to turn them against us. We should hatch a plot of our own, to ensure that [rival] focuses their ire on somebody else.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Moment of Change

options.text: Our pious ways inspire their people.
Not right now.

events.text: Our spies report that their contacts in [rival] and [rival] may be amenable to diplomatic discussions, improving relations with us. Where shall we activate our envoys?

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: More Than Allies

options.text: Provide [character] with the necessary supplies.
We share philosophies, but I cannot share my men.
[character] believes I am a fool.

events.text: Officers from the [rival] court have come to express their ruler's admiration and respect. [character], [title] of [rival], shares your belief in a strong military, and he sees wars with barbarian tribes as the single greatest threats to civilization. Would we be willing to place some of our soldiers under his command to assist [rival] in this ongoing struggle?

events.author: Zorbaz
events.name: Most Blessed People on Earth

options.text: You, of course! I'm surprised you even needed to ask.
You can't know if anyone is truly blessed until after they are dead.
Actually, it's me! I'm glad you asked.

events.text: We receive a letter from [character]: "Dear [character], Over the years you have acquired a great reputation for sagacity. I hope that you will therefore be able to answer a question for me. Of all people on earth, who is the most blessed?" The court strongly suspects that [character] is fishing for a compliment. Should we tell them what they want to hear?

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Not to Be Trusted

options.text: If that will assure you of peace, so be it.
Trust goes both ways, and there is little here, clearly.
You were right to fear [rival], [character].

events.text: [character] has seen [rival] actions and grown wary that relations might change at any moment. He proposes that young [character] reside as an honored guest of [rival], as a guarantee against future hostilities.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: Offensive Remarks

options.text: We will support an attack on [city].
We can offer supplies for an assault in the area of [city].
Both trust and manpower run short, I'm afraid.

events.text: [character] is planning an offensive against your shared enemy of [rival] and seeks to negotiate a shared plan of attack.

events.author: Jeri Roys
events.name: On a Platter

options.text: [character] has judged shrewdly. We cannot pass up this agreement.
[rival] shall stand on its own feet, or not at all.
[character] is a fool to flout his wealth so. Seize it, and ready the generals for war.

events.text: News of [rival] financial woes have apparently made it as far as [rival]. A [rival] ambassador arrives with a well guarded caravan carrying enough wealth to fill the royal coffers for years to come. delicately lays out the offer: [rival] will take up administration of the border city of [city], and in return [rival] shall receive the full military and financial support of the [rival] throne.

options.text: Send a generous gift to [rival], with our apologies.
Release [character] as ambassador for disrespecting [rival].
Surely [rival] understands that no offense was intended.

events.text: Our ambassador [character] is known for telling boastful stories, which some in the court have found tiresome, but harmless. During a recent state dinner with representatives of [rival], [character]'s proclivity for storytelling turned into a diplomatic incident. He was speaking about serving on the greatest court, with the best advisors and royals, which the [rival] took to be veiled insults of their own court. Unless you take immediate action, [character]'s attitude is likely to hurt our relations with [rival].
